::: {.key-question}

:::

## Belonging and Strength Through Culture and Community

### Cultural Knowledge and Wisdom

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Knowledge of culture
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
knowledge <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_Knowledge.csv")

# Data wrangling
knowledge <- knowledge %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(very_satisfied_n:not_at_all_satisfied_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(verysatisfied_n     = very_satisfied_n,
                notverysatisfied_n  = not_very_satisfied_n,
                notatallsatisfied_n = not_at_all_satisfied_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(verysatisfied_n:notatallsatisfied_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("verysatisfied"),
                starts_with("satisfied"),
                starts_with("neutral"),
                starts_with("notverysatisfied"),
                starts_with("notatallsatisfied"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "verysatisfied"     = "Very satisfied",
                                              "satisfied"         = "Satisfied",
                                              "neutral"           = "Neutral",
                                              "notverysatisfied"  = "Not very satisfied",
                                              "notatallsatisfied" = "Not at all satisfied",
                                              "answered"          = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Very satisfied",
                                           "Satisfied",
                                           "Neutral",
                                           "Not very satisfied",
                                           "Not at all satisfied",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Knowledge of culture - historical comparison
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
knowledge_2018 <- read.csv(file.path(root_folder, 
                                     "Population Health Data/ABS National Aboriginal Health Survey 2018-19/Data",
                                     "Aboriginal_IARE_Culture_Knowledge.csv"),
                           skip        = 9,
                           strip.white = TRUE) %>%
    #
    dplyr::rename(iare_name = colnames(.)[1]) %>%
    #
    janitor::clean_names() %>%
    #
    dplyr::filter(iare_name == "Melbourne") %>%
    #
    dplyr::mutate(iare_name = dplyr::case_when(
      iare_name == "Melbourne" ~ "Greater Melbourne",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>%
    #
    dplyr::select(iare_name,
                  everything(),
                  -ends_with("_rse"),
                  -ends_with("_annotations"),
                  -x) %>%
    #
    dplyr::rename_with(.fn = ~ paste0(., "_n"), .cols = 2:ncol(.)) %>% 
    #
    dplyr::mutate(across(!c(iare_name), as.numeric)) %>%
    #
    dplyr::mutate_if(is.numeric, ~ . * 1000)

# Data wrangling
knowledge_2018 <- knowledge_2018 %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(very_satisfied_n:not_at_all_satisfied_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(verysatisfied_n     = very_satisfied_n,
                notverysatisfied_n  = not_very_satisfied_n,
                notatallsatisfied_n = not_at_all_satisfied_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(verysatisfied_n:notatallsatisfied_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(iare_name,
                starts_with("verysatisfied"),
                starts_with("satisfied"),
                starts_with("neutral"),
                starts_with("notverysatisfied"),
                starts_with("notatallsatisfied"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!iare_name,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "verysatisfied"     = "Very satisfied",
                                              "satisfied"         = "Satisfied",
                                              "neutral"           = "Neutral",
                                              "notverysatisfied"  = "Not very satisfied",
                                              "notatallsatisfied" = "Not at all satisfied",
                                              "answered"          = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Very satisfied",
                                           "Satisfied",
                                           "Neutral",
                                           "Not very satisfied",
                                           "Not at all satisfied",
                                           "Total"))) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(iare_name == "Greater Melbourne")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 29% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that they were satisfied or very satisfied with their cultural knowledge. This equates to approximately 6,700 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- This was a decrease compared to the previous Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey conducted in 2018-19, where 34% (approximately 5,800 people) of survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that they were satisfied or very satisfied with their cultural knowledge.

- 44% of survey respondents (approximately 10,100 people) reported that they were not very satisfied or not at all satisfied with their cultural knowledge.

- Males were more likely to report that they were satisfied or very satisfied with their cultural knowledge than females (34% vs. 24%).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report, the impact of colonisation on low satisfaction with cultural knowledge was discussed.

- It was also noted that a large proportion of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples do not currently live on their homelands, which may also contribute to low knowledge of culture.

- It was also noted that how questions about cultural knowledge are asked and how the terms ‘culture’ and ‘community’ are interpreted can impact on how it is answered, including how individuals interact with community groups and how active they are within the community in which they live. Interpretation can also be influenced by age and stage of life, and trends over time could provide useful insights.

### Strength, Identity, and Belonging in Culture

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pride in culture
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
pride <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_Pride.csv")

# Data wrangling
pride <- pride %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(proud_of_culture_being_aboriginal_or_torres_strait_islander_n:not_proud_of_culture_being_aboriginal_or_torres_strait_islander_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(proud_n    = proud_of_culture_being_aboriginal_or_torres_strait_islander_n,
                notproud_n = not_proud_of_culture_being_aboriginal_or_torres_strait_islander_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(proud_n:notproud_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("proud"),
                starts_with("notproud"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>%
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "proud"    = "Yes",
                                              "notproud" = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 92% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that they were proud of their culture and/or proud of being Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander. This equates to approximately 21,400 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to report that they were proud of their culture and/or proud of being Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander than males (95% vs. 90%).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report it was discussed how the high proportion of respondents who were proud of their culture showed the positive impact of all the work that has been done in this area.

- It was considered that the small proportion who reported that they were not proud of their culture may be partially explained by people who have newly identified and may have a distorted perception of community that is influenced by the colonisation narrative.

- It was also noted that pride in culture does not necessarily correlate with connection to culture, and this relationship has more complexity than what may be displayed in these data. It is important to consider how these questions have been asked, how the survey was conducted, and how representative these data are as a result.

### Connection and Belonging to Nation, Language Group, or Clan

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Identification with tribal group, language group, or clan
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
identification <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_Identification.csv")

# Data wrangling
identification <- identification %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = total_n - not_applicable_n - not_known_n - refusal_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(tribal_n   = identifies_with_a_tribal_group_n,
                language_n = identifies_with_a_language_group_n,
                clan_n     = identifies_with_a_clan_n,
                mission_n  = identifies_with_a_mission_n,
                regional_n = identifies_with_a_regional_group_n,
                nogroup_n  = does_not_identify_with_tribal_group_language_group_clan_mission_or_regional_group_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(tribal_n:nogroup_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("tribal"),
                starts_with("language"),
                starts_with("clan"),
                starts_with("mission"),
                starts_with("regional"),
                starts_with("nogroup"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>%
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "tribal"   = "Tribal group",
                                              "language" = "Language group",
                                              "clan"     = "Clan",
                                              "mission"  = "Mission",
                                              "regional" = "Regional group",
                                              "nogroup"  = "No group",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Tribal group",
                                           "Language group",
                                           "Clan",
                                           "Mission",
                                           "Regional group",
                                           "No group",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 51% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that they did not identify with any specific tribal group, language group, or clan. This equates to approximately 11,100 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- 38% of survey respondents reported that they identified with a specific regional group and 27% reported that they identified with a specific tribal group.

- Females were more likely to report that they did not identify with any specific tribal group, language group, or clan than males (54% vs. 48%).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report, it was observed that these data may not be truly representative of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people. 

- Possible reasons for this lack of representativeness were: the purpose of this question may not have been clear to survey respondents, the wording of the question was not considered to culturally safe, and the mandatory nature of the survey would impact on the responses provided. Furthermore, these data would be heavily influenced by the ongoing impacts of the stolen generations.

### Being Recognised and Valued by Community

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Acceptance by members of community
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
acceptance <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_Acceptance.csv")

# Data wrangling
acceptance <- acceptance %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(feels_accepted_by_other_aboriginal_or_torres_strait_islander_people_n:does_not_feel_accepted_by_other_aboriginal_or_torres_strait_islander_people_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(accept_n   = feels_accepted_by_other_aboriginal_or_torres_strait_islander_people_n,
                noaccept_n = does_not_feel_accepted_by_other_aboriginal_or_torres_strait_islander_people_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(accept_n:noaccept_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("accept"),
                starts_with("noaccept"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>%
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "accept"   = "Yes",
                                              "noaccept" = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 75% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that they did feel accepted by other members of the Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Community. This equates to approximately 17,500 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples.

- Males were more likely to report that they felt accepted by other members of the Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Community than females (82% vs. 65%).

The following question was asked of all people aged 18 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

### Importance of Respect and Acknowledgement

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Importance of being recognised as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander 
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
recognition <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_Recognition.csv")

# Data wrangling
recognition <- recognition %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(very_important_n:not_at_all_important_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(very_n     = very_important_n,
                notvery_n  = not_very_important_n,
                notatall_n = not_at_all_important_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(very_n:notatall_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("very"),
                starts_with("important"),
                starts_with("neutral"),
                starts_with("notvery"),
                starts_with("notatall"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "very"      = "Very important",
                                              "important" = "Important",
                                              "neutral"   = "Neutral",
                                              "notvery"   = "Not very important",
                                              "notatall"  = "Not at all important",
                                              "answered"  = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Very important",
                                           "Important",
                                           "Neutral",
                                           "Not very important",
                                           "Not at all important",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 66% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that it was important or very important to them that they were recognised as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander. This equates to approximately 15,600 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to report that it was not at all important that they were recognised as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander than males (10%% vs. 4.6%).

  - Neutral
  - Not very important
  - Not at all important

## Connection to Country

### Recognition of Country

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recognition of homelands
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
homeland <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_Homeland.csv")

# Data wrangling
homeland <- homeland %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(recognises_homelands_n:doesn_t_recognise_homelands_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(homeland_n   = recognises_homelands_n,
                nohomeland_n = doesn_t_recognise_homelands_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(homeland_n:nohomeland_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("homeland"),
                starts_with("nohomeland"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "homeland"   = "Yes",
                                              "nohomeland" = "No",
                                              "answered"   = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 68% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that they recognised an area as their traditional Country. This equates to approximately 14,900 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males and females were equally likely to recognise an area as their traditional Country (68% vs. 68%).

### Connection Through Returning to Country

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Frequency of visits to homelands
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
visit <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Culture_HomelandVisit.csv")

# Data wrangling
visit <- visit %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(several_times_per_year_n:never_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(several_n   = several_times_per_year_n,
                annual_n    = once_per_year_n,
                notannual_n = less_frequently_than_once_per_year_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(several_n:never_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("several"),
                starts_with("annual"),
                starts_with("notannual"),
                starts_with("never"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "several"   = "Multiple times per year",
                                              "annual"    = "Once per year",
                                              "notannual" = "Less than once per year",
                                              "never"     = "Never",
                                              "answered"  = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Multiple times per year",
                                           "Once per year",
                                           "Less than once per year",
                                           "Never",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 69% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 18 years and over living in Greater Melbourne who recognised an area as their traditional Country do not currently live on their Country. This equates to approximately 10,300 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- 66% (approximately 6,800 people) of people who do not live on their traditional Country had visited, with 14% (approximately 1,400 people) visiting several times per year and a further 17% (approximately 1,800 people) visiting once per year.

- Females were more likely to visit their traditional Country several times per year than males (18% vs. 9.3%).

### First Nations Rights and Responsibilities for Lands and Waters

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 15](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/land-and-waters/): Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people maintain a distinctive cultural, spiritual, physical, and economic relationship with their land and waters**

Target A: By 2030, a 15% increase in Australia’s land mass subject to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests.

Target B: By 2030, a 15% increase in areas covered by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests in the sea.
:::

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Land mass where native title exists
# Data from Native Title Determinations Outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Native Title data
nativetitle_land <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(root_folder, subfolder_ctg, "CTG15_Land_Waters_Data_Tables.xlsx"),
                                       skip  = 1,
                                       sheet = "Table CtG15A.1") %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(model = x2,
                value = x3,
                type  = x4,
                year  = x5) %>%
  #
  tidyr::fill(model, value, type) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(model == "Actual" & type == "Total area") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(vic)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(value,
                year,
                vic)

# Data wrangling
nativetitle_land <- nativetitle_land %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(vic = as.numeric(vic),
                #
                value = dplyr::case_when(
                  value == "Land area" ~ "land_n",
                  TRUE ~ "land_prop")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = "value",
                     values_from = "vic") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(land_target_n    = 14934 + (14934 * 0.15),
                land_target_prop = 6.6 + (6.6 * 0.15))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sea area where native title exists
# Data from Native Title Determinations Outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Native Title data
nativetitle_sea <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(root_folder, subfolder_ctg, "CTG15_Land_Waters_Data_Tables.xlsx"),
                                      skip  = 1,
                                      sheet = "Table CtG15B.1") %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(value = x3,
                type  = x4,
                year  = x5) %>%
  #
  tidyr::fill(value, type) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(value == "Actual") %>%
  dplyr::filter(year %in% c("2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(value = type,
                year,
                vic = vic_b)

# Data wrangling
nativetitle_sea <- nativetitle_sea %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(vic = as.numeric(vic),
                #
                value = dplyr::case_when(
                  value == "Sea area" ~ "sea_n",
                  TRUE ~ "sea_prop")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = "value",
                     values_from = "vic") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(sea_target_n    = 265 + (265 * 0.15),
                sea_target_prop = 2.6 + (2.6 * 0.15))

# Join land and sea data
native_title <- nativetitle_land %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(nativetitle_sea, by = "year")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/), compiled from the [National Native Title Tribunal Geospatial Data Model](https://www.nntt.gov.au/assistance/Geospatial/Pages/Spatial-aata.aspx).

- In 2024, 7.2% of Victoria’s land mass (approximately 16,351km^2^) was subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests, an increase from 6.6% (approximately 14,934km^2^) in 2020. This was below the Closing the Gap target of 7.6% (approximately 17,174km^2^).

- In 2024, 2.9% of Victoria’s sea area (approximately 295km^2^) was subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests, an increase from 2.6% (approximately 265km^2^) in 2020. This was below the Closing the Gap target of 3.0% (approximately 305km^2^).

- Detailed maps of areas covered by native title claimant applications, native title determinations, and Indigenous Land Use Agreements can be found on the [National Native Title Tribunal website](https://www.nntt.gov.au/assistance/Geospatial/Pages/Maps.aspx).

:::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Figure 7A-5

::: {#fig_7A_5 .fig-tab-title}
**Figure 7A-5:** Percentage of land mass and sea area subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people's legal rights or interests on June 30th, by year
:::

```{r}
#
figure_count <- figure_count + 1

figure_percent <- native_title %>% 
  dplyr::select(year,
                land_prop,
                sea_prop) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols     = !year,
                      names_to = "prop") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(category = dplyr::recode(prop,
                                         "land_prop" = "Land mass",
                                         "sea_prop"  = "Sea area"),
                #
                hover_text = paste0(year, "\n",
                                    category, "\n",
                                    "Percentage: ", sprintf("%.1f", value))) %>%
  #
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, group = category, col = category, text = hover_text)) +
  #
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +
  #
  geom_hline(data = native_title,
             aes(yintercept = land_target_prop),
             col       = colour_landmass,
             linetype  = "dashed",
             linewidth = 1) + 
  #
  geom_hline(data = native_title,
             aes(yintercept = sea_target_prop),
             col       = colour_seaarea,
             linetype  = "dashed",
             linewidth = 1) +
  #
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 10),
                     breaks = scales::breaks_width(1),
                     expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.125)),
                     labels = scales::comma_format(big.mark = ",")) +
  #
  scale_color_manual(values = c(colour_landmass, colour_seaarea),
                     labels = c("Land mass", "Sea area"),
                     name   = NULL) +
  #
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = NULL) +
  #
  theme_classic()

figure_percent %>% 
  plotly::ggplotly(tooltip = "text") %>% 
  #
  plotly::layout(hovermode = "x",
                 #
                 yaxis = list(title = list(text     = "Percentage of land mass or sea area",
                                           font     = list(size = 13, family = "Arial"),
                                           standoff = 10)),
                 #
                 legend = list(x = 0.5,
                               #
                               orientation = "h",
                               xanchor     = "center"))
```

:::: {.callout-note title="Data notes" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/), compiled from the [National Native Title Tribunal Geospatial Data Model](https://www.nntt.gov.au/assistance/Geospatial/Pages/Spatial-aata.aspx).
  - The Closing the Gap Information Repository brings together data from a wide range of data sources to provide up to date information for each Closing the Gap target, indicator, and contextual factors.
  - The National Native Title Tribunal Geospatial Data Model brings together information about native title claimant applications, native title determinations, Indigenous estates, registered and notified Indigenous Land Use Agreements, and registered native title bodies corporate.

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Total land mass, total sea area, and the percentage subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests are calculated based on jurisdictional boundaries sourced from [Geoscience Australia](https://www.ga.gov.au/scientific-topics/national-location-information/dimensions/area-of-australia-states-and-territories).

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Land mass subject to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people’s legal rights or interests includes:
  - Determinations of native title (land subject to a determination that native title exists exclusive or non-exclusive)
  - Indigenous estates (land grants under various land rights regimes of the states and territories and the Commonwealth)

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- The Closing the Gap targets are marked with a dashed green line (land mass) and a dashed blue line (sea area) in Figure 7A-5.
